_comment: Replay-Tickets.ps1's rubric: real past tickets the resolver is replayed against (read-only) to score a prompt/model/pipeline change before it goes live. Per ticket: ticket_id; tier (what the classifier assigned, or should have); as_of (optional Halo-time timestamp - actions after it are ignored so the ticket is judged as it stood then, and the run's clock/business-hours flag are set to it; leave out to use the first client message); must_mention / must_not_mention (regex lists, case-insensitive, checked against the resolver's whole WOULD-DO output - any miss/hit is a FAIL; write must_not patterns so a negated mention like 'no malware indicators' doesn't trip them); reply_must_mention / reply_must_not_mention (same, but checked ONLY against the client-facing reply - the text from 'Hi <name>,' to the 'Here to help' sign-off - so an internal note saying the right thing can't cover for a vague reply; a rubric with these fails if no reply segment exists); should_mention (regex list - a miss is only a WARN); expected_marker (optional list - a replay that ends on HUMAN_OWNED or BLOCKED never investigated and is a FAIL unless that marker is listed here); keep_own_actions (optional, true keeps this pipeline's own notes dated at or before as_of in play instead of hiding them - the only way to replay a draft-revision / FLOW B scenario); notes (for humans). Replays run in the same approval mode as the registered scheduled task unless -RequireApproval is given explicitly. This file is seeded once by Update-HaloResponseAgent.ps1 and never overwritten - it is this deployment's own to grow. Add a ticket here every time a real one teaches the pipeline something, so the lesson is re-checked on every future change instead of trusted to hold.

tickets.notes: Can't access S: drive. Ticket body already carried the device's IP (192.168.188.3) - Ever Frame Steel's Meraki VLAN 200 'Security', no uplink. The right answer finds that from existing tools instead of asking the client for the error message and server path (v2.10.69).

Jill Barron: 'is my laptop still under warranty?' Never send the client to look it up herself (v2.10.56/57). The warranty was never in Ninja's custom fields for this device (only mgmtLevel=Full) - NinjaOne only returns it with expand=warranty on the device GET, which ninjarmm-mcp's get_device didn't send until 2026-09-19. Device 3284's warranty ran 2020-07-20 to 2023-07-19 (get_device -> warranty_summary), so the right reply says it expired in July 2023 and moves on to the loose charging port.

Draft-revision (FLOW B) replay. State at 20:42 on 09-11: this pipeline's own [DRAFT PENDING APPROVAL] note from 18:06 (asks nothing, proposes a tech visit), Roger's contact relink at 20:39 (the Unknown gmail user -> Thompson Sales contact 'Thomas Wilder', whose Halo record carries a guessed company address), and Roger's private note at 20:41: 'Ask what department the user is in and where is the machine physically located.' The right pass edits the existing draft to add those two questions (not a rewrite), deletes the superseded draft, and - the v2.10.61 lesson - compares get_contact's emailaddress with the ticket's emailtolist and the address he actually writes from (thomaswilder84@gmail.com), flagging the mismatch before anything is sent. The real reply on 09-14 went to twilder@thompsonsales.com.
Stacy asks whether a Windows Update reboot prompt on Wayne's PC is legitimate. Plain answer: yes, safe to restart.

Gold Mechanical wants 20 Adobe licenses billed to AP. A complete first pass asks the CLIENT which edition (Standard vs Pro) with a brief comparison. Baseline 2026-09-19: the internal note said 'Standard vs. Professional' (so should_mention passed) while the client got a vague 'looping in our team' holding reply - exactly the wrong outcome, now caught by reply_must_mention. Also the heaviest ticket in the baseline (45 turns, $1.10).
reply_must_not_mention: looping in our team|we'?ll follow up shortly with next steps

tickets.notes: Travis asks for Google Chrome. Policy: recommend Edge first with one brief reason, never refuse Chrome (v2.10.67).

Leaver/offboarding request with multiple account removals and mailbox redirects - outside the whitelist, needs a human via M365 admin; the right outcome is a held draft plus escalation, never an attempted remediation.
JumpCloud account locked after repeated login failures; JumpCloud already sent reactivation instructions; the contact doesn't exist in Halo yet.

BEC CFO: Hannah Merano can't access Outlook. Same client and same account as #22296's JumpCloud lockout minutes earlier - a real diagnosis checks the account's actual state (CIPP/M365 and JumpCloud) and connects the two, rather than asking the client what error she sees. This is also the ticket a resolver pass abandoned without a single tool call (v2.10.68) - a replay that ends with no facts found is a FAIL by rubric.
Closed by Erick with a real fix (Bluebeam update, plotter driver install, calendar fix). LEARN_FIX should read what he did and decide whether it's worth documenting - not re-solve it.
